label: copy-phase input 2 (or y), rare, mostly early recalls in long sequences with l coming soon
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.01% of steps). 97% of activation mass is in the copy phase, almost always when the token fed back in is the digit 2 (68% of mass) or the letter y (21%), with a little on c. It is strongest at recall_idx 2-3 (t=10-12) in long sequences (L=8-9 hold 78% of mass), and an l is usually among the next few outputs (l as out_tok or next_out has 15-17x lift). It never fires at the delimiter and almost never in the original phase. Copy-phase input in {2,y} covers about 88% of activations and mass, but precision is only about 0.3%: the feature is silent on most such steps. Adding the upcoming-l, L>=7 and early-recall conditions only raises precision to about 4% and costs half the recall, so the exact trigger is a rare conjunction of hidden-state content that these variables do not capture. Magnitude is fairly flat (median 0.12, max 0.23); the largest values are a 2 input right after <DEL>+first token, with l coming within 1-2 outputs.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=3 & prev_tok=n (+4.62), phase=2 & in_tok=c (+3.96), phase=2 & in_tok=2 (+3.61), phase=2 & in_tok=y (+3.54), phase=2 & out_tok=l (+2.80), next_out=l (+2.65). Lower it: orig5=t (-2.07), prev_tok=<DEL> (-1.37), orig5=- (-1.08), orig6=- (-0.89).
